She got fired for paying for an old man's juice.
It was pouring rain when the old man walked in. Patched sweater. Soaking wet. A handful of coins.
He counted them on the counter. One dollar and forty cents. The cheapest juice was two dollars.
He smiled, said sorry, and turned to leave.
Peaches stopped him. She took sixty cents out of her own tip jar, and made him the biggest juice on the menu.
He didn't say a word. He just looked at her name tag. For a long time.
Then Mr. Lemons stormed out of the back.
Did you just give away free juice to some broke old man?
I paid for it myself, sir.
You're done. Clean out your locker.
Peaches cried the whole walk home. Rent was due Friday.
The next morning, a black car pulled up in front of the store. The old man stepped out. Same patched sweater. But this time, four men in suits were holding umbrellas over him.
The old man walked right past him.
I founded this company fifty years ago. I visit one store a year, dressed like this, to see who we really are.
Then he handed Peaches a sealed envelope.
Don't open this until I'm gone.
What's in the envelope? Comment your guess. Part two tomorrow.
